hook.line: Vale wants cheaper flour, and every shop on the street has a sign in the window. Tomás has to know which signs mean a real deal.

rule:
Three easy ways to talk about a deal.

*Estar en oferta* (or *en promoción*): the thing is on sale. No article after *en*.

*Tener un 20 % de descuento* or *hay un descuento del 15 %*: the discount itself.

*Estar rebajado*: the price has been cut. It describes the thing, so it matches it: *rebajada*, *rebajados*.

And *salió más barato* (or *más caro*) says how it worked out afterwards.

In Spain you'll hear *las rebajas*. In Colombia, *oferta*, *promoción* and *descuento* are more usual.
smallPrint: *Rebajado* is a past participle used as an adjective, so it agrees like one.

options: The shirt is reduced in price.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *rebajada* or *rebajado*: La camisa está ___. Type the whole sentence.
Choose *rebajada* or *rebajadas*: Las camisas están ___. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: *Las camisas* is feminine and plural, so *rebajadas*.
The discount is something it *has*: *tiene un 20 % de descuento*.
Same *en oferta*, now as a question.
*Salió* tells how it worked out, then *más barato*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say the opposite: Salió más barato.

pitfalls.why: Almost. After *en*, Spanish drops the article.
